title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth, connected projective variety of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, with ℓ ≠ char k. Write Alb°_X for the Albanese variety and Pic^{00}_X = (Pic^0_X)_red for the reduced Picard variety; these are dual abelian varieties (previous page: B_X = Pic^{00}, A_X = B_X^*). π_1 means the ℓ-adic Tate module, and (t) means 'up to torsion'. The page lists four comparisons between the ℓ-adic cohomology of X and that of its Albanese and Picard varieties.

(1) The Albanese map X → Alb induces π_1^ab(X)(ℓ) → T_ℓ(Alb). This is an isomorphism up to torsion. Poincaré duality gives π_1^ab(X)(ℓ) = H_1(X,Z_ℓ) ≅ H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n), again up to torsion. Grothendieck asks whether the map to T_ℓ Alb is always surjective.

(2) T_ℓ(Pic^{00}) ≅ H^1(Alb,Z_ℓ)(1) by Weil-pairing duality. Pulling back along the Albanese map gives H^1(Alb)(1) → H^1(X)(1), an isomorphism up to torsion. This is compatible with the previous page's H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ T_ℓ Pic^0.

(3) Untwisted, the same statement reads H^1(Alb) → H^1(X), with the question whether it is always injective.

(4) H^1(Pic^{00}) ≅ T_ℓ(Alb)(-1), again by duality of abelian varieties. Up to torsion this is isomorphic to H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). This repackages the exact sequence of the previous page, 0 → (NS(X)[ℓ])^∨ → H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1) → H^1(B_X,Z_ℓ) → 0.

Conclusion: if abelian varieties are labelled by their H^1, then Alb_X corresponds to H^1(X) and Pic_X corresponds to H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). In motivic terms, h^1(X) = h^1(Alb_X) and h^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) = h^1(Pic^0_X). This is the standard identification of the 'Picard' and 'Albanese' pieces of the motive, and the dictionary between abelian varieties up to isogeny and weight-one (effective) motives. The purpose is to place the abelian varieties attached to X inside the cohomological and motivic framework of the cycles and standard-conjectures notes.
errors: Not a real error: the 'torsion près' qualifier on the H^1 comparisons in (2) and (3) is over-cautious. With Z_ℓ coefficients, H^1(X,Z_ℓ) = Hom(π_1(X),Z_ℓ) is torsion-free. Since π_1^ab(X)(ℓ) → T_ℓ Alb is surjective with finite kernel, H^1(Alb,Z_ℓ) → H^1(X,Z_ℓ) is a genuine isomorphism.

The marginal questions have standard affirmative answers. π_1^ab(X) → π_1(Alb) is surjective for normal projective X (Lang–Serre theory of the Albanese; finiteness of the kernel e.g. in Katz–Lang 1981). Hence the dual map H^1(Alb) → H^1(X) is injective, indeed bijective.
Minor notational slip: the last line writes Alb_X without the ° used elsewhere on the page.

ideas.what: T_ℓ Alb is isomorphic, up to torsion, to π_1^ab(X)(ℓ) ≅ H^{2n-1}(X)(n); dually, H^1(Alb) ≅ H^1(X)
ideas.modern_name: Albanese map induces isomorphism on H^1 / abelianized ℓ-adic π_1 modulo finite kernel
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang, Serre (1950s); Grothendieck's FGA/SGA period; Katz–Lang 1981 for finiteness statements
ideas.where_published: Related material in FGA exposés on Picard scheme and SGA1 (π_1); not stated in exactly this form

ideas.what: H^1(Pic^{00}) ≅ T_ℓ Alb(-1) ≅ H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), up to torsion
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré duality plus Weil pairing; Picard/Albanese motive identification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil; formalized motivically by Grothendieck (via Kleiman 1972, Demazure) and Murre (1990)
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 'Motives' (1972) and Murre 'On the motive of an algebraic surface' (1990) contain the motivic version

deep.surprise_reason: A clean summary of standard facts relating H^1 and H^{2n-1} to the Albanese and Picard varieties. The open questions it raises are answered affirmatively by known results, and the motivic dictionary is the well-known one.
transcription_corrections: First line: '(t) H^{2n-1}(X)(n)' is written above the arrow and attached to π_1^ℓ(X)^ab(ℓ), not inserted inline; the bracket '{: torsion près}' qualifies it.
Last formula line: the trailing word appears to be a crossed-out 'toujours' (scribbled over), consistent with the [-toujours-] deletion.
'Si on répère' should read 'Si on repère'; the manuscript spelling is ambiguous.
